high.title: Ibovespa Falls with Uncertainty Over US-Iran Negotiations; 5 Things to Know Before Investing Today (21)
high.summary: The Ibovespa is tracking negative external sentiment amid geopolitical uncertainties, falling 0.64% to 176,228.08 points by 10:10 AM Brasília time. The USD/BRL is strengthening, with the dollar rising 0.25% to R$5.0159, following broader dollar strength as measured by the DXY index (+0.26% to 99.354 points). Political uncertainty continues as Flávio Bolsonaro's pre-campaign coordinator stepped down amid controversy over funding requests. This selloff reflects risk-off sentiment in emerging markets as investors await clarity on US-Iran negotiations, which could impact global commodity flows and risk appetite. The combination of political noise domestically and geopolitical tensions internationally is weighing on Brazilian assets. FX traders should monitor if USD/BRL breaks above the R$5.02 level, while equity investors should watch for any recovery in risk sentiment or further deterioration if geopolitical tensions escalate.

high.title: Petrobras (PETR4) Adheres to Fuel Subsidy Program, Eye on Pricing Policy
high.summary: Petrobras' board of directors approved the company's participation in the economic subsidy program for fuel producers and importers under Provisional Measure 1,358. The subsidy mechanism provides tax refunds for gasoline and diesel producers/importers, enabling Petrobras to implement fuel price adjustments with reduced impact at gas stations amid rising oil price pressures. This move is strategically important as it allows the state-controlled oil giant more pricing flexibility while maintaining political acceptability during a period of elevated crude prices. For equity investors, this reduces political risk around Petrobras' pricing policy and supports margin protection. The subsidy program demonstrates government support for maintaining fuel price stability, which is crucial for inflation control and monetary policy effectiveness.

medium.title: Petrobras (PETR4), Azzas 2154 (AZZA3), J&F SA and Other Highlights This Wednesday (20)
medium.summary: Brazil's Federal Court of Accounts (TCU) concluded that Petrobras executed a financial policy in 2024 misaligned with its strategic planning, paying dividends 88% above estimates and debt payments 49% higher than projected, while investments fell 39% below targets. This analysis highlights concerns about capital allocation at the state oil company and could influence future dividend expectations and investment planning for PETR4 shareholders.

medium.title: B3 Opens Exception for BradSaúde (SAUB3) in Novo Mercado; See What Changes
medium.summary: B3 granted temporary exception to BradSaúde to remain in Novo Mercado segment despite not meeting minimum free float requirements, allowing 8.6% free float until October 2027. The company accepted enhanced governance measures including separate minority shareholder board representation. This flexibility in listing requirements demonstrates B3's pragmatic approach to maintaining companies in premium segments while protecting minority investors.

medium.title: US Weekly Unemployment Claims Fall Amid Labor Market Resilience
medium.summary: US initial jobless claims fell by 3,000 to 209,000 in the week ended May 16, showing labor market resilience and giving the Federal Reserve room to focus on rising inflation. Markets expect the Fed to maintain rates at 3.50%-3.75% range. Additionally, US-Iran-Israel conflict has disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, boosting oil and commodity prices. This impacts Brazilian markets through commodity price channels and Fed policy expectations affecting EM flows.
